fields.name: operation
fields.label: Operation / Sub-command
fields.desc: Dispatch byte read via ldrb at internal struct offset +0x14 (20) on both architecture builds. Selects one of three structurally different sub-layouts for the rest of the payload: operation=1 ('port switch') uses only byte1=switch_mode and replies synchronously via duss_event_resp_data_without_retcode with a 2-byte {return_command=1, return_code=0} ack; operation=2 ('route switch', detailed in the remaining fields below) is forwarded asynchronously to an internal queue with no immediate ack payload; operation=3 ('switch done') uses byte1=link_mode and byte2=type and replies synchronously with a 2-byte {return_command=3, return_code=0} ack. Any other value falls to a default branch logging 'RS: unsupport rs command :%#x' and returns an internal error code (-1001) with no wire response constructed at all.

fields.desc: Read via ldrb at struct offset +0x19 (25). Used directly both as the loop bound for, and to decide whether to execute, the host_id_list array below (confirmed on both architecture builds: a cmp/bls-style bound check against this exact byte gates the per-entry 'RS: route switch host id = %#x' log loop).

fields.name: host_id_list
fields.label: Host ID List (operation=2 only)
fields.type: uint16[] (little-endian, 2 bytes per element, repeated host_id_count times)
fields.desc: Array of little-endian 16-bit host IDs starting at struct offset +0x1a (26), each individually logged via 'RS: route switch host id = %#x'. 2-byte element stride independently confirmed on both builds: AArch64 indexes as `ldrh w4,[x28, x27, lsl #1]` with x28 = base+0x1a; ARM32 indexes identically as `ldrh.w r2,[ip, #26]` with ip = base + (index*2). Total field size is 2*host_id_count bytes; the size shown here (2) is for a single element.
